claims.text: A W-Ta-Nb alloy, optionally containing a minor Mo addition, can serve as an effective interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed refractory HEA interlayer can bridge the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed refractory HEA interlayer can suppress interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed interlayer can enhance the mechanical integrity of the W/CuCrZr interface under fusion-reactor conditions.
Refractory HEAs can exhibit thermal stability in extreme or hostile environments.
A directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface suffers from severe thermal-expansion mismatch.
A directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface has poor adhesion.
Interdiffusion degrades directly bonded W/CuCrZr interfaces under extreme conditions.
A refractory HEA interlayer can possess a nanocrystalline or finely structured microstructure.
The proposed W-Ta-Nb(+Mo) interlayer will have a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The proposed W-Ta-Nb(+Mo) interlayer will provide robust diffusion-barrier properties.
Suppressing interfacial diffusion will prevent formation of brittle intermetallic layers at the W/CuCrZr interface.
Mediating the thermal-expansion mismatch will reduce interfacial stress concentrations during thermal cycling.
The interlayer will reduce interfacial cracking and degradation during cyclic high-temperature exposure.
The interlayer will improve bond strength and retained mechanical integrity relative to a directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface.
A nanocrystalline refractory HEA can resist irradiation-induced defect evolution and detectable grain growth.
